data.name: Hilf
data.gender_notes: Hilf is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Hilf is derived from the Arabic root 'h-l-f', which means 'to help', 'to support', or 'to aid'. In Islamic contexts, Hilf can be understood as a spiritual aid or a source of assistance. It is a reminder of Allah's promise to help and support His believers in times of need. The name Hilf carries the meaning “Support, Aid, Assistance” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hilf usually hope their child will grow to embody support, aid, assistance and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Encourages one to seek assistance from Allah and others when in need
data.etymology: Hilf belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Support, Aid, Assistance.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hilf total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hilf holds cultural significance as a symbol of unity and solidarity among Muslims. In Islamic history, the term Hilf al-Fudul refers to a pact or an agreement made between the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and some of his earliest companions. This agreement was aimed at providing mutual support and protection to each other against any form of injustice. The name Hilf can also be used to refer to any kind of communal or social assistance or aid, reflecting the Islamic value of sharing and helping one another.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Hilf can be seen as a reminder of the divine aid and support that Allah provides to His believers. The Quran states, "And We have sent you (O Muhammad) with the truth as a bearer of good news and a warner. And there never came to them a messenger but they mocked him. So We sent for them a successive host of possessors of judgement and wealth. And We sent them an inspiration of Our Commandment. But they believed not therein"(Arrahman 105:3-5). This verse emphasizes that Allah sends guidance and assistance in various forms, despite the disbelief and mockery of some people.

historical_references.reference: The Hilf al-Fudul was an alliance formed between the Prophet Muhammad and a group of clans from the Banu Aus and Banu Khazraj in Medina. This pact was made in order to protect the early Muslim community from harassment by the Meccan Quraysh. The name 'Hilf al-Fudul' translates to 'The Pact of the Virtuous'. This event is recorded in Sahih Bukhari, a collection of hadith compiled by Imam Bukhari.
historical_references.context: Protection pact between Prophet Muhammad and Banu Aus and Banu Khazraj clans

historical_references.reference: The Hilf al-Rasheedah is a reference to a famous saying of Aisha bint Abi Bakr, who narrates that when the Prophet Muhammad migrated to Medina, he made an alliance with the women of Medina. This pact was known as Hilf al-Rasheedah or 'The Pact of the Righteous Women'. The objective of this pact was to support the Prophet Muhammad and defend Islam. The women pledged to obey the Prophet and his companions in all matters, including matters of jihad. This event is recorded in Sahih Muslim, a collection of hadith compiled by Imam Muslim.
historical_references.context: Alliance between Prophet Muhammad and women of Medina
